clue.text: Welsh town in which the leaves drop

definitions.meaning: a county town in south-west Wales, with a famous castle
a small table of that name has hinged flaps that hang down when not in use

explanation.surface: An autumn scene in a Welsh town where the trees are shedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaves are not on trees but the hinged flaps of a table that fold down.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a place in Pembrokeshire; the same name is given to a drop-leaf table design.

clue.text: Record I have left, for one of a later generation

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
gone means departed, left

explanation.surface: A family archive: a recording someone has left for their descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigone is a lesser follower or imitator from a succeeding generation.

clue.text: It's not made up — that's obvious

definitions.meaning: a face with no make-up is a bare face
undisguised, blatant, as in a shameless lie

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a face has no cosmetics, and that this is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the word describes a face without make-up; idiomatically it means shameless and open.

clue.text: Mysterious officer in charge of religious system

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
a cult is a system of religious worship

explanation.surface: A commanding officer who belongs to a strange sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult means hidden, secret, beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Shanty for young sweeps?

parts.note: sweeps are long oars and their rowers; the young rowers are pupils at a famous English school whose song celebrates rowing

explanation.walkthrough: Young sweeps suggests boy chimney sweeps; here a sweep is a long oar. Eton is an English boarding school on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A song sung about rowing by boys at Eton, the English public school, is a sort of shanty for young oarsmen.

clue.text: Grab high-sounding honour

indicators.note: sounding tells us to take a word as it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word high, as spoken
in bridge the jack is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: Seizing a lofty-sounding award.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the honours are the ace, king, queen, jack and ten of trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize or commandeer, especially a vehicle.

clue.text: Use stolen iron to smooth out cloth

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
to press is to iron

explanation.surface: Advice to a thief to put a pilfered iron to work on fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-pressing flattens and glazes cloth or paper between heated plates.

clue.text: Like one joining a non-voluntary movement, a Continental

parts.note: as means like
I is the Roman numeral one
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Describing a European who joins an unwilling march.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the continent of Asia; asiatic as a noun means a native of Asia.

clue.text: Royal Horse Artillery is a killer in the jungle

parts.note: a king is royal
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A regiment of mounted gunners is deadly in jungle warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Horse Artillery is a real regiment, which hides the split into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous snake is a lethal predator of South Asian forests.

clue.text: An acid critic right out of place

indicators.note: out of place says a letter is moved to another position in the word critic

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued reviewer whose remarks are inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An acid critic' reads as a harsh reviewer, but 'acid' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Citric acid is the sour compound found in lemons and limes.

clue.text: He looks you in the eye, producing a coin tip

definitions.text: He looks you in the eye

indicators.note: producing suggests the letters are brought out and made into something new

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone making eye contact while handing over a coin as a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges A COIN TIP into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist examines your eyes to test sight.

clue.text: Greens here form group after whip round.

indicators.note: after puts the group's word behind the other piece
round tells us to turn the word for whip about

parts.note: to flog is to whip
a club is a society or group

explanation.surface: A society forms after a collection is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip round' looks like a British collection of money; 'round' turns FLOG into GOLF. Greens are putting surfaces on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting greens are found at a golfing association's course.

clue.text: Countryman's dog retrieved out of its turn

indicators.note: out of here means placed outside another piece
retrieved, read as brought back, turns the word for dog round

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: turn says the word its is read the other way

explanation.surface: A farmer's dog fetches something when it should not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrieved' gives RUC (CUR backwards), 'turn' gives STI (ITS backwards), and 'out of' puts RUC around STI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a country dweller, a simple rural person.

clue.text: It may be shingled or combed by a man

definitions.text: It may be shingled or combed by a man

parts.words: It may be shingled or combed by a man
parts.note: reads like hair being cut short or groomed, but means a seashore covered with pebbles or searched by a scavenger

explanation.definitionFit: Shingle covers many seashores, and a beachcomber searches the shore for finds.

clue.text: Doubly qualified old fool the first to eye this woolly creature

indicators.note: doubly tells us to take the degree abbreviation twice

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, shows someone is qualified
coot is an old word for a silly person

indicators.note: the first to picks out the opening letter of eye

explanation.surface: A twice-graduated old fool is first to spot an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The babacoote is the indri, a large woolly lemur of Madagascar.

clue.text: It sounds an admirable vehicle for the back-seat driver

definitions.text: It sounds an admirable vehicle for the back-seat driver

indicators.note: sounds says the phrase that follows is taken as heard

parts.note: a good-looking carriage, said aloud

explanation.surface: A fine-sounding car for someone who nags the driver from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The back-seat driver is not a nag: the driver of this two-wheeled carriage really did sit high up at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, with the coachman perched behind.

clue.text: After the battle, almost disregard the priest

indicators.note: after puts the battle first, with the other piece following it

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was a First World War battle

indicators.note: almost removes the last letter of the synonym

parts.note: to ignore is to disregard

explanation.surface: Once the fighting is over, pay no attention to the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A title given to senior Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Old sailor's ship, half novel submarine

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, a link to the wordplay

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

indicators.note: half keeps only the first four letters of the submarine's name

parts.note: Nautilus is Captain Nemo's submarine in Verne's novel

explanation.surface: An ancient mariner's vessel is half a fictional submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the heroes who sailed with Jason in quest of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: A booby, obviously

parts.note: a booby is a fool but also a seabird, which naturally has the brain of a bird

explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person is called a featherhead; a booby, being a seabird, literally has one.

clue.text: Party wear in favour

definitions.meaning: a ribbon badge worn by election candidates and supporters
a favour is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge

explanation.surface: Wearing an outfit to a party when it is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon cockade is worn to show party allegiance and was given as a favour.

clue.text: Some infant rattles can produce cavities

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A warning that babies' toys might cause tooth decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity such as a sinus.

clue.text: Regroup in large formation

indicators.note: formation suggests the letters of in large being drawn up anew

explanation.surface: Troops reorganising into a big formation.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to arrange again or form new alliances.

clue.text: French dog is perhaps rabid? Right!

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a French hound is foaming at the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A briard is a large shaggy French sheepdog.

clue.text: Game with chips? This is the place to visit!

definitions.text: Game with chips? This is the place to visit!

parts.words: Game with chips? This is the place to visit!
parts.note: chips suggests food, but they are gambling counters at a gaming house

explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is where games are played for chips; it is also the name of a card game.

clue.text: A gremlin developing in revolutionary calendar

definitions.note: the answer is a month found in that calendar, so in describes its place

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters of a gremlin are changing into something new

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite causing trouble in a radical new calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges A GREMLIN. The French Revolution introduced its own calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh month of the French Republican calendar, in spring.

clue.text: A repeated phrase, one the Western allies applied to E German

parts.note: Ost is German for east
I is the Roman numeral one
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation alliance

explanation.surface: Cold War politics: the Western alliance and East Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an ostinato is a short motif persistently repeated.

clue.text: A free BBC

parts.note: to untie is to free

explanation.surface: A complaint that the broadcaster ought to be free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Broadcasting Corporation is nicknamed Auntie, or Auntie Beeb.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar nickname for the British national broadcaster.

clue.text: Actors go off in this direction

definitions.text: Actors go off in this direction

parts.words: Actors go off in this direction
parts.note: direction means not a compass point but a stage instruction telling performers to leave

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage instruction meaning 'they leave'.

clue.text: In headlong flight from a grenade explosion

indicators.note: explosion suggests the letters of a grenade are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Fleeing in a hurry from an exploding bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges A GRENADE. The word recalls the Gadarene swine rushing into the sea in the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadarene describes a headlong rush, after the biblical swine that charged down a slope.
